Festive

/FES-tiv/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Festive means suited to a celebration; joyful and lively in atmosphere.

Strings of red lanterns and drumming in the square gave the whole street a festive glow for the new year.

Worked Example

The overnight ferry to the islands is usually a quiet ride of dozing commuters. But on the night of the solstice run, the crew strings fairy lights along the rails, an accordion player sets up near the snack bar, and passengers pass around tins of ginger cookies with strangers. Same boat, same route — but for one night the whole crossing turns festive.

The lights, live music, and shared cookies transform an ordinary crossing into one with a joyful, celebration-ready atmosphere — which is precisely what festive describes.

How Festive Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

merry

merry: cheerful and full of good spirits

jolly

jolly: happily good-humored

Antonyms

gloomy

gloomy: dark and cheerless

funereal

funereal: grimly solemn, like a funeral

How Strong Is It? — pleasant → festive → exuberant

pleasant vs. festive

pleasant vs. festive: Pleasant describes any agreeable atmosphere; festive means the air itself feels dressed for a celebration.

exuberant vs. festive

exuberant vs. festive: Exuberant is stronger than festive — the joy is not just in the decorations and mood but overflowing from the people themselves.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — fest

Root — fest: feast, holiday (Latin festum)

Suffix — -ive

Suffix — -ive: having the quality of

Put it together

Put it together: Festive comes straight from Latin festum, 'feast or holiday' — the root that also throws festival, fiesta, and feast itself. Add -ive, 'having the quality of,' and festive means 'having the quality of a feast day': lights up, music on, the ordinary rules of a gray afternoon suspended.

Use the root in a new word: festival

Use the root in a new word: festival: A festival is a whole event built around communal joy — the same Latin root festum, 'feast or holiday,' that makes an atmosphere festive.
